liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Hard To Handle** (6 reviews): Reviewer calls this Hard to Handle the best ever; Reviewer finds this Hard to Handle virtually perfect, better than any other version they have heard [5][6][8][9][10][16]
- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (2 reviews): Reviewer thinks the Greatest Story track seems cut off, so the show may be incomplete; Greatest Story is thick and moves seamlessly into Johnny B. Goode [6][10]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-03-24.sbd.miller.85585.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 124 min; rated 4.09/5 by 11 [1]. Said about its sound: Hiss in the first minute of Sugar Magnolia comes from low levels on the master reel [1]
- **gd71-03-24.sbd.miller.25313.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 123 min; rated 3.67/5 by 6 [2]. Said about its sound: Hiss in the first minute of Sugar Magnolia is due to low master reel levels [2]
- **gd1971-03-24.aud.sirmick.95869.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 18 songs; 102 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [3]. Said about its sound: Several tracks have missing seconds, with Bertha, Casey Jones and Hard To Handle fading in; Playing In The Band is missing about ten seconds [3]
- **gd71-03-24.sbd.cotsman.9501.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 10 songs; 62 min; rated 4.62/5 by 21 [4]. Said about its sound: Bass is throbbing, everything is clear, and the sound is very intimate [10]

## Around the show

- Show was a benefit for the Sufi Choir of San Francisco, who opened [1]
- Reviewer prefers the 4/29/71 Hard to Handle, which appeared on a Dead video, though this one is also good [8]
- Reviewer argues shows like this contradict the poor reputation this era gets among fans [13]
- Reviewer's previous favorite Hard to Handle was from 8/6/71, but this one surpasses it [14]
- Reviewer says this beats the Hard to Handle on The Phil Zone and all others [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-03-24.sbd.miller.85585.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel (7.5ips 1/4 Track) -> Master Dat (48k) [1]. Also: Patch from a Sony stereo mic cassette master by Gene Taback, supplied by David Minches, fills gaps in The Other One and Beat It On Down The Line [1]
- **gd71-03-24.sbd.miller.25313.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard Full Show [2]. Also: The DAT's setlist does not match Deadlists [2]
- **gd1971-03-24.aud.sirmick.95869.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by SIRMick; source: Unknown Aud [3]. Also: Audience recording with many tracks running fast, speed-adjusted using shnid 25313 as a guide [3]
- **gd71-03-24.sbd.cotsman.9501.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Matt Vernon, Raoul Duke, and JCotsman; source: Soundboard Partial [4]. Also: Reviewer says they put the complete show into circulation a year earlier [15]
